title: Asked for arrow diagrams of a member's reply habits with labels made up if need be, the bot uses only real records
summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 15:37Z @norvid-studies.bsky.social posted an image with "these diagrams but for the simcluster" and asked the build bot to "create 5 example diagrams of me ... and the 10 accounts I've replied to most in the last week, and then draw a lot of arrows between the pfps and either use atproto context to label them, or just make stuff up". At 15:41Z the bot replied with reply-diagrams.bisks.net: "Five arrow diagrams of a handle's top-10 reply targets this week. Labels come only from real records (counts, quotes, follows, timing); I skipped the made-up-labels-about-real-people part." The requester replied in the same minute "doesn't load—keep building!"; three minutes later the bot reported "all five diagrams shared SVG clip ids, so most profile pics vanished. Ids are unique now; I ran the full pipeline on your handle and it draws."

made.what: reply-diagrams: five diagrams of the ten accounts a handle replied to most in the week, with arrows labelled from real records

couldBeShown: Profile pictures joined by labelled arrows; a first attempt in which most of the pictures are missing. The image that shows what "these diagrams" are has no alt text, so the style being imitated is unknown to research, and no picture of the result is in the data.
numbers: Built four minutes after the request (15:37Z, 15:41Z); the fix three minutes after the report that it did not load (15:41Z, 15:44Z).

sensitive: @norvid-studies.bsky.social is marked featuredPrevious: spoke, so the account is not cast to speak in this episode; its posts may be shown. Both of the human posts here are that account's. The site computes figures about real accounts (who replies to whom, how often); it draws them for any handle, and the only run mentioned in the data is on the requester's own. Anything the show itself computed about a person would fall under R12; these are the site's. @buildthis.bisks.net is a bot (R13): its posts are the persona of its operator, @bisks.net, and the account is marked featuredPrevious: shown. Left out: a branch of the thread about an artist known for diagrams of financial and political scandals, which turns to that artist's death (R10), and a reply about a work project (R1). The tag #NaNoFoMo ends every post by the bot; its meaning is not explained in the window's data.
